text: 1.关于信息茧房你需要知道
en: 1. What you need to know about information cocoons

text: 什么是信息茧房
en: What is an information cocoon

text: 又称回声室效应,指在新闻和社交媒体上,拥 有相近想法的群体借由不断沟通与认同彼此想法，使得那 些相似的想法不断被放大与加强，进而忽略甚至不相信世 界的多样性。
en: Also known as the echo chamber effect, it refers to groups with similar ideas on news and social media continuously communicating and affirming each other's ideas, so that those similar ideas are constantly amplified and strengthened, thereby ignoring or even disbelieving the diversity of the world.

text: 一叶障目，不见泰山。
en: A single leaf blinds the eye, hiding Mount Tai.

text: 自我验证理论、和确认性偏见指出，茧房是往往自己制造的。
en: Self-verification theory and confirmation bias point out that cocoons are often self-made.

text: （“兼听则明，偏信则暗”并不容易做到）
en: (Listening to both sides makes one enlightened, trusting only one side makes one benighted — is not easy to achieve.)

text: 推荐算法让你很容易在网上找到一个心理上互相支持的网络，并因此变得过度自信。
en: Recommendation algorithms make it easy for you to find a psychologically mutually supportive network online, and therefore become overconfident.

text: 2. 信息的特点
en: 2. Characteristics of information

text: 信息的本质是对不确定性的度量，信息的价值是消除不确定性。
en: The essence of information is a measure of uncertainty; the value of information is eliminating uncertainty.

text: 通过关注信息增量，而不是存量，可以极大提高效率。
en: By focusing on information increments rather than stock, efficiency can be greatly improved.

text: 或 者说“不同点”包含更大的信息量。
en: Or rather, 'differences' contain greater amounts of information.

text: 一流的智慧存在于顶级大佬的脑袋里，二流的思想交流于 普通大佬们的小圈子里，三流的技术“老师”愿意收费/免费卖给你。
en: First-rate wisdom exists in the heads of top big shots; second-rate ideas circulate in the small circles of ordinary big shots; third-rate technical 'teachers' are willing to sell to you, paid or free.

text: 门槛的高度与信息的优质程度往往成正比。
en: The height of the threshold is often directly proportional to the quality of the information.

text: 在信息传输过程中，由于噪声和其他干扰，熵增是确定发生的。
en: During information transmission, due to noise and other interference, entropy increase definitely occurs.

text: 如果对信息不做选择,随波逐流或者平均地分配注意力，系统会变得越来越无序。
en: If you do not select information, drift with the tide, or distribute attention evenly, the system will become increasingly disordered.

text: 3. 破茧而出的道：良好的习惯事半功倍
en: 3. The way to break out of the cocoon: good habits yield twice the result with half the effort

text: 比做什么更重要的不做什么，离开高噪声源：以传播情绪为主的短视频平台
en: More important than what to do is what not to do: leave high-noise sources — short video platforms mainly spreading emotions.

text: 批判性思维看待问题
en: View problems with critical thinking.

text: 优质输出倒逼优质输入
en: High-quality output forces high-quality input.

text: 付费的本质是买时间，有时很划算
en: The essence of paying is buying time; sometimes it is very cost-effective.

text: 绝技：从被动输入到主动搜寻信息很重要
en: Secret skill: moving from passive input to actively searching for information is important.

text: 5.AI工具——==普通人的能力倍增器==
en: 5. AI tools — == a capability multiplier for ordinary people ==

text: 先挖个坑，有关AI工具的使用，后续会写文章分享
en: Digging a hole first: regarding the use of AI tools, I will write articles to share later.

text: 少看油管、谷歌，假信息太多，西方管控太严。
en: Watch less YouTube and Google — too much false information, Western control too strict.

text: 学会真正的独立思考。
en: Learn true independent thinking.

text: 最近一直陷入一个怪圈，沉浸在自己的信息茧房里，看了一些关于信息茧房的推文，感觉很在理，摘抄分享给大家
en: Recently I have been stuck in a strange loop, immersed in my own information cocoon. I read some tweets about information cocoons, felt they made sense, and excerpted them to share with everyone.

text: 现在互联网已成为人们获取信息的主要渠道，搜索引擎的智能化、社交媒体的普及以及个性化推荐算法的广泛应用，在为人们带来便捷的同时，也在不知不觉中促成了信息茧房的形成。
en: Now the internet has become the main channel for people to obtain information. The intelligentisation of search engines, the popularisation of social media, and the wide application of personalised recommendation algorithms have brought convenience to people, while also unconsciously promoting the formation of information cocoons.

text: 首先，大家要知道信息茧房是什么。
en: First, everyone should know what an information cocoon is.

text: 信息茧房指人们的信息领域会习惯性地被自己的兴趣所引导，从而将自己的生活桎梏于像蚕茧一般的“茧房”中的现象。
en: An information cocoon refers to the phenomenon where people's information fields are habitually guided by their own interests, thereby confining their lives in a 'cocoon' like a silkworm's.

text: 一方面，个性化推荐算法根据用户的浏览历史、搜索记录和社交关系等数据，为用户精准推送他们可能感兴趣的内容。
en: On the one hand, personalised recommendation algorithms precisely push content users may be interested in based on data such as users' browsing history, search records and social relationships.

text: 另一方面，在社交媒体平台上，人们往往倾向于关注与自己观点一致的人，加入与自己兴趣相符的群组。
en: On the other hand, on social media platforms, people tend to follow people with views consistent with their own, and join groups matching their interests.

text: 其次，你要知道信息茧房的害处。
en: Second, you should know the harms of information cocoons.

text: 它限制了人们的认知视野、使得思维变得狭窄，影响对事物的准确判断；不利于创新思维的培养，更可能对社会和谐稳定造成威胁，当不同群体之间的信息交流和理解越来越少，彼此间的隔阂和误解就会加深，加剧社会的分裂和对立。
en: They limit people's cognitive horizons, narrow thinking, and affect accurate judgment of things; they are not conducive to cultivating innovative thinking, and may even threaten social harmony and stability. When information exchange and understanding between different groups become less and less, the barriers and misunderstandings between them deepen, aggravating social division and opposition.

text: 很赞同后者微信推文的观点，现在社会的最大问题是“傻X共振”现象太严重，平台“算法”的产生又加剧了这个现象，你越喜欢什么就越给你推荐什么。
en: I very much agree with the latter WeChat article's view: the biggest problem in society now is the 'idiot resonance' phenomenon being too serious, and the emergence of platform 'algorithms' has aggravated this phenomenon — the more you like something, the more it recommends it to you.

text: 它让每个人都沉溺在自己的世界里，每个人只能看到自己喜欢看、愿意看的东西，于是人们视野变的越来越狭窄、观点变的越来越偏激。
en: It makes everyone indulge in their own world, where everyone can only see what they like and are willing to see, so people's horizons become narrower and narrower, and their views more and more extreme.

text: 也就是说，如果你只关注自己愉悦的东西，久而久之便会像蚕一样，将自己桎梏于自我编织的茧房之中，从而丧失看清真相的能力。
en: That is to say, if you only focus on things that please you, over time you will be like a silkworm, confining yourself in a cocoon woven by yourself, thereby losing the ability to see the truth clearly.

text: 最后，告诫大家，世界很大、多出去走走，不要沉浸在自己的网络世界中，“作茧自缚”！
en: Finally, a word of advice to everyone: the world is big — go out and walk around more, don't immerse yourself in your own online world, 'weaving a cocoon to trap yourself'!

text: 参考1：浙江宣传微信号：打破信息茧房：在数字时代拓展认知边界
en: Reference 1: Zhejiang Publicity WeChat account: Breaking Information Cocoons: Expanding Cognitive Boundaries in the Digital Age

text: 参考2：互联网思维微信号：现在社会最可怕的现象：傻 X 共振
en: Reference 2: Internet Thinking WeChat account: The most frightening phenomenon in society now: idiot resonance

text: 信息茧房的本质，是共鸣（或共情）成瘾。
en: The essence of an information cocoon is resonance (or empathy) addiction.

text: 避免活在信息茧房中的唯一路径，就是戒除这种成瘾。
en: The only path to avoid living in an information cocoon is to quit this addiction.

text: 这里有一些相对简单的训练方法：
en: Here are some relatively simple training methods:

text: 1、学会解析信息及其包含的逻辑的底层，通过对信息的极简化处理，去掉形容词和各种诱发情绪的褒义词，把底层逻辑暴露出来，从而在规避共鸣（或共情）的情况下，进行真伪和程度性的检查。
en: 1. Learn to parse information and the underlying logic it contains; through extreme simplification of information, removing adjectives and various emotion-inducing laudatory words, expose the underlying logic, so that under the avoidance of resonance (or empathy), truth and degree checks can be carried out.

text: 2、使用合订本模式，有意识的跟踪曾经对自己产生巨大共鸣，或巨大情绪刺激的信息，在热点消退和自己的情绪消退后，进行分析、复盘，寻找当时自己的共鸣点产生的原因和带来的认知偏差，以及思考如何在未来规避这种偏差。
en: 2. Use the bound-volume model: consciously track information that once produced huge resonance in you, or huge emotional stimulation, and after the hotspot fades and your emotions fade, analyse and review it, looking for the causes of your resonance at the time and the cognitive biases it brought, and thinking about how to avoid such biases in the future.

text: 3、有意识的寻找认可的信息或观点的对立面，并分析其合理性的程度。
en: 3. Consciously seek the opposite of recognised information or views, and analyse the degree of its rationality.

text: 4、反向代入，即不仅仅代入条件反射的立场和角色，也代入与之对立的角色。
en: 4. Reverse role-play: not only role-play the reflexively conditioned stance and role, but also the opposing role.

text: 5、极化推断，即将信息及其逻辑，向极端化方向推演，看是否出现明显谬误。
en: 5. Polarised inference: push information and its logic towards extremes, and see if obvious fallacies appear.

text: 如果有明显谬误，再反推当前信息及其逻辑的适用范围或真伪。
en: If obvious fallacies appear, then infer back the applicable scope or truth of the current information and its logic.

text: 6、非从众意识，寻找与你一样共鸣的人的共同特点和特征，并且推断，如果去掉这些特征，该信息是否还会被认可。
en: 6. Non-conformist awareness: find the common characteristics and features of people who resonate like you, and infer whether the information would still be recognised if these features were removed.
